paragraphs: Friend, here's what I love about this psalm. David doesn't pretend. He tells God he's crushed, he tells God his spirit is faint, and he even admits that "no one alive is righteous before You" (Psalm 143:2). He doesn't bring his résumé to prayer, he brings his need. If the king of Israel prays like that, you can pray like that on your worst day too.

Now watch what David does with the hard stuff. He looks back at what God has already done and reaches out for Him like a parched land reaching for water (Psalm 143:5-6). Then he asks for something bigger than rescue: "Teach me to do Your will, for You are my God" (Psalm 143:10). I think that's the heart of the whole thing, because David wants to be led, not just fixed. And he trusts that God's "good Spirit" can lead him "on level ground" (Psalm 143:10).

So here's your takeaway, baker. When life is heavy, don't go quiet, go TO God, and go with an open hand and an open ear. Ask Him to teach you, and then keep showing up in the morning to listen (Psalm 143:8). I spent years in the dark, and I can tell you this: asking to be taught by God beats trying to figure it all out alone, every single time.
